newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria mulls steps to secure autumn sowing.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria mulls steps to secure autumn sowing.

text.p: Cash-strapped Bulgaria, hit by a severe wheat shortage, is considering parliamentary measures to provide badly needed funds for securing the autumn sowing, the state news agency BTA reported on Wednesday.

"Parliamentary spokesman Blagovest Sendov, central bank governor Lyubomir Filipov, agricultural ministry officials and deputies for the ruling Socialists gathered to discuss urgent measures to provide funds for the autumn sowing," the BTA said.

According to a report presented at the meeting by the agriculture ministry, only 250,000 ha of wheat and barley have been sown, while the country needs to sow some 1.6 million ha by November 5 to cover domestic consumption, BTA reported.
If the planned 1.6 million ha were sown, that would secure 5.5 million tonnes of grain for the following year, Socialist deputy Kosta Andreev said, quoted by the agency.

The group will present a proposal for providing funds for the sowing with preferential interest rate, Andreev said. The option that the state should guarantee the credits had also been discussed, he added.
A draft bill will be presented to parliament on Friday.

Bulgaria has delayed the autumn sowing due to the record high interest rate and because farmers' funds are blocked in banks which have been placed under special supervision. Bad weather has also hampered the sowing.

Bulgaria raised its main interest rate to an all-time high of 300 percent annually and put nine banks under special supervision on September 23 in a bid to stabilise its crumbling financial sector and support its ailing currency, the lev.
Local newspapers say nearly four billion levs belonging to farm cooperatives are blocked in those banks.
"We are considering ways to unblock the farmers' funds in the nine banks put under special supervision," Andreev said, quoted by the agency.
Last year Bulgaria sowed one million ha with wheat and 270,000 ha with barley.
Officials say Bulgaria is looking for different options for barter deals to meet its grain needs for this year.
